top_experiments.experiment: PMMA film 0.2 mm, 1 cm wide, 21.0% O2, 101.3 kPa
top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: Record shows 3 tests at 21.0% O2 and 101.3 kPa with flow reduced until extinction ('extinction (flow reduced)'). Report states thin PMMA flames (100-300 um) extinguished by radiative extinction at opposed flows of about 1 cm/s, with critical velocity ~10 mm/s at 21% O2.
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: Demonstrates that reducing ventilation below ~1 cm/s can extinguish flames on thin solid films at 21% O2. Inferred: at higher lunar-base O2 (30-34%), lower flow would likely be needed to sustain or extinguish flames, but this was not tested.
top_experiments.why_selected: Maps opposed-flow flame spread and radiative extinction limits for thin solid PMMA film.

top_experiments.experiment: PMMA film 0.1 mm, 2 cm wide, 21.0% O2, 101.3 kPa
top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: Record lists 3 tests at 21.0% O2 and 101.3 kPa with varied fan/air settings. Report states steady leading-edge flame spread rate of 2.2 mm/s over 100 um (0.1 mm) PMMA film at 20.7% O2 and 1 atm.
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: Provides baseline microgravity flame spread rate (2.2 mm/s) for thermally thin solid fuels, matching 1g downward spread. Inferred: lunar-base habitats with 30-34% O2 would experience faster spread rates than this 21% O2 baseline.
top_experiments.why_selected: Provides directly measured steady flame spread rate over thin solid PMMA film.

top_experiments.experiment: SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, 1 cm wide, 21.0% O2, 101.3 kPa
top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: Record lists 4 tests at 21.0% O2 and 101.3 kPa. Report states concurrent-flow quenching speeds for SIBAL fabric were 1-5 cm/s (higher at lower O2, varied 21% to 16%), though the 1.2-cm-wide quenching limit was not fully resolved.
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: Establishes ventilation thresholds below which composite fabric fires self-quench in microgravity. Inferred: relevant to textiles in habitats, though lunar partial gravity and elevated O2 would alter convective quenching limits.
top_experiments.why_selected: Covers concurrent flame growth, spread, and quenching on a practical spacecraft fabric.

similarities: All three ran at 21.0% O2 and 101.3 kPa in microgravity.
All three tested thermally thin solid fuels.
differences: Fuel type and geometry: PMMA films (0.1-0.2 mm) vs. SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric.
Flow configuration: opposed flow (CS02, CS07) vs. concurrent flow (CS68).
top_experiments_comparison.conclusion: Together, these experiments show that thin solid fuels spread steadily at ~2.2 mm/s in 21% O2 and quench at low forced flows (1-5 cm/s). Evidence is strong for 1 atm microgravity, but does not cover lunar-base O2/pressure or partial gravity.

top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: 4 tests at 70.0 kPa and 30.0% O2 with no suppressant: 3 ended in Disruption, 1 in Completion. Mean initial diameter 3.34 mm, mean extinction-to-initial ratio 0.17, mean burning rate 0.635 (table units labelled 'mm', likely mm^2/s).
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: At lunar-base-like 30.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa, methanol droplets did not self-extinguish early (3 disruptions, 1 completion). Inferred: high-O2, reduced-pressure lunar habitats leave very little margin for self-extinction.
top_experiments.why_selected: Directly tests 30.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa lunar-base-like conditions.

top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: 5 tests at 70.0 kPa and 34.0% O2 with no suppressant: 4 ended in Disruption, 1 in Completion. Mean initial diameter 3.46 mm, mean extinction-to-initial ratio 0.37, mean burning rate 0.654.
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: At 34.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa, methanol droplets burned vigorously to disruption or completion with no radiative extinction. Inferred: upper lunar-base O2 levels pose severe fire-prevention challenges.
top_experiments.why_selected: Tests upper 34.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa lunar-base-like conditions.

top_experiments.summary_of_key_findings: 4 tests at 70.0 kPa and 30.0% O2 with no suppressant: all 4 ended in Disruption. Mean initial diameter 3.28 mm, mean extinction-to-initial ratio Not available, mean burning rate 0.66.
top_experiments.fire_safety_interpretation: Sooting hydrocarbon (heptane) droplets at 30.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa all ended in disruption rather than extinction. Inferred: like methanol, hydrocarbon fuels will not self-extinguish at lunar-base O2/pressure.
top_experiments.why_selected: Provides sooting hydrocarbon data at 30.0% O2 and 70.0 kPa.

overall_insights: BASS-II (PSI-25) provides direct solid-material flame spread rates (e.g., 2.2 mm/s for 0.1 mm PMMA) and low-flow quenching limits (1-5 cm/s), but only at 1 atm and <=22.2% O2.
FLEX (PSI-69) covers lunar-base-like 70.0 kPa and 30-34% O2, showing liquid droplets burn to disruption or completion without extinguishing, but provides no solid-fuel or flame-spread data.
gaps: No solid-material flammability or flame spread rate data at raised-O2 (30-34%), reduced-pressure (~70 kPa) lunar-base conditions.
No partial-gravity (lunar 1/6 g) data in either investigation; both are microgravity only.
caveats: PSI-25: Tested at ~21% O2 or below and ~1 atm; no data at raised-O2, reduced-pressure lunar habitat conditions; microgravity only.
PSI-25: Flow speeds are free-text fan/air display sequences, not converted to cm/s.
PSI-69: Lunar Base tag is inferred from conditions, not stated in FLEX documents.
PSI-69: Burning-rate column is labelled 'mm' in the table (probably mm^2/s); extinction diameter of 0 treated as no measurable extinction diameter.
